Ankita is quick and friendly with customers. One thing I noticed: whenever someone asks for a cough syrup or a pain balm, she reaches for the product from the television adverts first and says, 'This is the best one.' Same ingredients, same amounts. She went red and laughed. 'I just trusted it because I've seen it a thousand times.' Next step: from Monday she will read labels aloud to me before suggesting any product, and when customers need advice she will call the pharmacist.

Saturday

Did a stupid test with Vidya today. I've bought the same instant coffee for four years, the one from the TV ads with the mountain. I told her it's obviously better than the plain shop-brand jar she buys. She said, 'Prove it.' She made two cups without telling me which was which. I tasted both, three times, very seriously. Picked cup B as 'mine'. It was hers. The cheap one. I didn't believe her, so we did it again. I picked wrong again. Vidya didn't gloat much. Walking home, I kept thinking: I never actually compared. I just saw the mountain ad a thousand times and the jar felt like a friend. That's not the same as it tasting better. I'm still buying mine this month. But I'm less sure why.

Chinmay

passage: You asked how I became the person who eats anything, Gautam. Honestly, I'm Urmila, and I used to be the fussiest eater in my family. Last year I noticed something: every food I 'loved' was something I'd had since I was five. Every song on my playlist was from school. Even my friends were all from the same colony. It made me wonder if I liked things, or just knew them. So I made a rule: three fair tries before I decide. The first time I ate Naga pork with bamboo shoot, I hated the sourness. The second time, less. The third time I asked for more. The same with a Portuguese singer my colleague played, and with a quiet guy at work I'd written off. He's now one of my closest friends. Some things I still don't like after three tries, and that's fine too.

qa.a: It gives new foods, music or people a fair chance to become familiar before judging, while still allowing a real dislike after three tries.

qa.a: He may feel glad and valued that Urmila gave him another chance and got to know him.
